items: Newer Epic games now install: games whose download uses Epic's newer format (like Agent A) no longer say "This game uses a download format Fishy Client can't install yet."
Encrypted games still can't be installed; Fishy Client now says so right away instead of getting stuck at 0%.
Safer self-update: Update now double-checks that it's installing a newer version, so an older one can never be installed.
The title bar is solid black: nothing shows through it any more.
A game started from its desktop shortcut no longer turns Fishy Client's taskbar icon into the game's icon.

Note on Launch options: Fishy Client passes your words to the game, but each game decides whether it understands them. Many games ignore them, and each engine uses different words (for example -windowed works for Unreal games, while Unity games use -screen-fullscreen 0 and may still keep their own setting).
Every installed game has a Manage box: open a game's ⋯ menu and pick Manage….
Auto update for each game: it follows the switch in Settings until you change it for that game.
Priority download: that game's downloads go to the front of the waiting list.
Shortcut: put the game on your desktop (and, if you like, in the Start menu). Clicking it opens Fishy Client and starts the game.
Verify checks every file of a game and downloads only the missing or damaged ones.
Launch options: extra words added when the game starts, like -windowed.
Downloads has Start now for waiting games: pause the one that's downloading, or download both at once.
Boxes like What's new and Install no longer slide under the title bar.
Fishy Client has its own fish-style title bar instead of Windows' white one: drag it to move the window, double-click to maximize.
Lighter while you play: the waves and fish pause while Fishy Client is minimized or a game you started from it is running, then swim on when you come back.
Click a game's cover to open its own page, with its buttons, size and playtime.
A game's page shows your Epic achievements: which ones you have, when you got them, and how rare the others are. Switch between All, Unlocked and Locked.
Open game folder in a game's ⋯ menu opens its files in Windows Explorer.
Fishy Client now counts how long you play games you start with it; the ⋯ menu shows it ("Played: 12 h 5 min").
The Store says "In your Library" for a free game you already have, instead of offering Get on Epic.
New Store page: this week's free games and the ones coming next, with Get on Epic to claim them on Epic's own page.
Open Epic's store shows Epic's real store in a Fishy Client window. Your sign-in there is remembered until you log out of Fishy Client.
A game you get or buy in the Store window shows up in your Library when you close the window.
Scrollbars now match the app: thin, square and aqua instead of Windows' grey ones.
Fortnite installed with Epic's launcher can now be added, with the parts Epic installed (Save the World and LEGO Fortnite come along). Fishy Client reads which parts you have from the files on disk.
Updating Fortnite in Fishy Client downloads only the parts you have, plus any brand-new part. Epic's launcher keeps working too; updating in one may make the other update again.
Games with optional parts that aren't installed yet are installed with Epic's launcher first: Fishy Client then adds them by itself.
Downloads can be faster: each download first tries all of Epic's download servers for a moment and uses the fastest. If a server fails, the next one takes over.
When a download speed limit is on, the Downloads page says so ("Limited to 1 MB/s") with a link to change it in Settings.

You can install games into Epic's own folder (C:\Program Files\Epic Games): press Use Epic's folder in the Install box or in Settings. Windows asks for permission once per game, the same way Epic's launcher does.

Games another store installs, such as STAR WARS Battlefront II through the EA app, now show in your Library with "Installs through the EA app" instead of under Not on Windows. Fishy Client can't install or start those: use Epic's launcher or the EA app.
Games you haven't installed look a bit greyer in the Library, so your installed ones stand out more.
Games you already installed with Epic's launcher can be added without downloading them again: press Add them at the top of the Library.
If some of their files are missing or damaged, Download them fetches only those.
Fishy Client can now update itself: when a new version is out, a bar offers Update now (you can turn the check off in Settings).
The ⋯ menu of an installed game shows how much space it takes.
The Install box warns about folders that need administrator rights, such as C:\Program Files\Epic Games.
Games you haven't installed look a bit grey in the Library.
The Install box says that Epic's launcher can't see games installed with Fishy Client.
This What's new box.
The first version: sign in with Epic, see your Library, install, play and update your games.
Pause and resume downloads, with a speed limit if you want one.
Library filters and sorting, and a Running badge while a game is open.
Settings, logs without secrets, and Delete all my data.
A Windows installer (.msi).
